items.title: Chuck Findley interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 6, 2023
items.q: Because my brother was my idol and still is, he’s eight years older than me, my brother Bob... he would take me to gigs when I was fourteen... he’d sit at the bar and have a beer and he knew everybody in the band. And he was so proud of me you know.

ctx.x: Man, I mean that one performance sort of encapsulates what you’re capable of with the soloing and the respectful treatment of the melody and then some really high, high notes. So when you think of “Close to You” and that performance is one harder than the other?

I’d say “Close to You” was harder, only because I wasn’t free to improvise on anything like that. It had to be done note by note. Right? I mean on “Nature Boy” I was free to do whatever I pleased to do. So I could — every night I had to play it so I’d play it different every night. You know, it wasn’t that I had to do it — and of course the melody you play but the melody also is not just the melody the way I’d play it the night before. I’d play it differently every night, ‘cause that’s what an artist does or at…

Yeah. Let me ask you about that because I heard you talking about that and that your dad would play in restaurants and he would stroll, he’d pick up the violin and maybe stroll around. And I wondered, did you and your brother Bob actually witness that? Did you go to these places?
